approvalMessage.text:
APPROVAL MEMORANDUM - No. 88 Chapter 716
 
       MEMORANDUM filed with Assembly Bill Number 126-A, entitled:
 
    "AN  ACT to amend the public health law, in relation to establishing
        a list of emerging contaminants"
 
    APPROVED
 
  This legislation expands the list of chemicals to be included  on  the
emerging  contaminants  (ECs) list, and requires regulations updating be
issued within 90 days and every three years. These would be additions to
the chemicals tested for by  the  state,  counties,  municipalities  and
those private entities that own public water systems.
 
  In  2017,  the  "Emerging  Contaminant  Monitoring  Act," was enacted,
creating a standard list of chemicals that must be tested by all  public
water  systems.  The  federal  standard  list  of chemicals (Unregulated
Contaminant Monitoring Rule  (UCMR)-3),  issued  by  the  EPA  in  2012,
included  many  chemicals already found in New York. However, it did not
require testing by all water systems. By the passage of this  bill,  and
the testing for these chemicals in all water systems, New York will gain
a better understanding of the levels of exposure.
 
  This  legislation  is a valuable piece in protecting our water sources
but the input of the Drinking Water Quality Council is crucial to a full
understanding of these chemicals including how to address them. To  that
end,  I  have  come  to  an agreement with the legislature on amendments
which would allow the Council to review a number of these that are  less
known, so that chemical testing and notification can be more effective.
 
  With that agreement, I am pleased to sign this legislation.
 
  This bill is approved.                         (signed) KATHY HOCHUL

                                ______

summary: Relates to adding additional chemicals to the list of emerging contaminants; directs the commissioner of health to establish the first list within 90 days and to update the list every three years.
